title: Occupational therapy
what: A specialist helps you get back skills for everyday life: dressing, eating, washing, writing, cooking. They suggest aids for the home.
why: After a stroke or injury, with joint conditions, and for children with developmental issues, when daily tasks are hard to manage alone.
duration: a session usually lasts 45 to 60 minutes; the specialist decides on the course
tell_doctor: Any pain, dizziness, or vision problems
How your home is laid out: steps, bathtub, thresholds

prepare.title: Goals
prepare.text: Think about what you most want to do on your own again. That is where you will start.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes and the shoes you usually wear.

bring: Glasses, a hearing aid, or a cane, if you use them
A family member who helps you at home
steps: The specialist asks what is hard for you to do
They watch how you do everyday tasks
You practice movements and skills in the session
The specialist suggests aids and changes at home
feel: Tasks can be tiring. Take breaks
It should not hurt. Tell the specialist
after: Practice the skills at home every day
Family should not do everything for you, but help a little at a time

faq.q: How is occupational therapy different from physical therapy?
faq.a: Physical therapy trains muscles and movement. Occupational therapy trains specific tasks: dressing, eating, washing.

faq.q: Should I bring a family member?
faq.a: It is a good idea. They will learn how to help you at home the right way.

reminders.text: Occupational therapy tomorrow. Bring your reports and the things you use every day.
